notes: This source/test traceability contract covers the bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Publish Object Class Directed Interactions service in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable development profile. The focused production-filesystem regression rejects undefined object and interaction class designators without appending a successful-void report, then verifies an accepted declaration with ObjectClassHandle type 36 and InteractionClassHandleSet type 28. It also verifies that a supplied empty interaction-class set remains a successful §5.6 no-op and is recorded as an empty Array<InteractionClassHandle>, not as an absent argument. The report is appended only after the registry accepts the declaration. The Requirements Lab assigns the coalesced §5.6 body candidates to clause-5.6.3; RL-078 records that source-ownership mismatch while this contract retains the direct §5.6 source context. Table 5's rotated InteractionClassHandleSet row has no row-level Requirements Lab candidate (RL-067/RL-076); its exact Array<InteractionClassHandle> form and the static MIM type-28 enumerator are retained in implementation comments and focused source/API traceability. Complete directed delivery matrices, subscriptions/unsubscriptions, timestamped/retraction behavior, DDM, public MOM delivery, remote transport, packaging, validation, and conformance remain outside this slice.
